title: Single Orangutan Moms Set up Playdates for Their Kids - Nautilus
gist: Female orangutans raise offspring alone for six to eight years, teaching them to access roughly 250 food items, and a new PNAS study finds they go to great lengths to arrange playdates for their young.

insights.claim: Male orangutans contribute only genetic material to their offspring and then leave, so female orangutans raise their young entirely alone.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Background on the extreme maternal investment in orangutan development.
insights.quote: They contribute nothing more than genetic material to their offspring before disappearing back into the forest.
insights.locator: Being a single mom is tough

insights.claim: Orangutan mothers spend six to eight years teaching their young skills such as termite fishing and fruit picking, covering around 250 food items needed for independent survival.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Illustrates the long, learning-intensive childhood of great apes, relevant to the study of social learning.
insights.quote: That leaves mom to teach their kids how to fish for termites, pick fruit, and access the other 250 odd food items that will allow them to survive on their own.
insights.locator: Being a single mom is tough

insights.claim: A new study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences finds that orangutan mothers go to great lengths to arrange playdates for their offspring despite the heavy workload of teaching them.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
entities: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
insights.so_what: Suggests social play is valued enough in great apes that mothers invest scarce time and effort to secure it.
insights.quote: orangutan moms go to great lengths to set up playdates for their youngsters
